findings.title: Polygon, BNB Chain and Avalanche nodes are built with Go releases that carry an open prove miscompile of narrow sign extensions
findings.difference: The endpoints report bor/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 (Polygon), Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 (BNB Chain), avalanchego/1.15.3 with go=1.26.10 (Avalanche) and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817/linux-amd64/go1.24.13 (Celo op-geth). The release files agree: bor v2.11.1 Dockerfile uses golang:1.26.10-alpine and go.mod says go 1.26.10, avalanchego v1.15.3 go.mod says go 1.26.10, bsc v1.8.2 builds from golang:1.26-alpine, and celo op-geth c7ed55b8 from golang:1.24-alpine3.22. Go issue 82839, opened 2026-11-03 and still open, reports that the prove pass carries a fact through a sign extension with a 32 bit constant that does not fit the 16 bit type and takes a branch that cannot be taken, on any GOARCH, for go1.26.6 through go1.26.10, go1.27.3 and master; the report says a variant form is wrong from go1.24.13 to go1.26.x, and that the go1.26.6 backport of the fix for issue 80517 made the shown form reach the faulty code. go1.26.11 and go1.27.4 of 2026-11-10 list compiler fixes, but the issue was open on 2026-11-17 and the fix CL 858581 is not shown as merged. Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain run go1.27.3 and Elysium go1.25.12 (F-136), which fall in the same stated range.
findings.mechanism: A node compiled by an affected toolchain computes a wrong branch only where its own Go code compares a sign-extended narrow integer with a constant wider than the narrow type. The EVM paths the PoolManager depends on (256 bit arithmetic in holiman/uint256, jump destination analysis, memory and copy offsets) work on uint64 words; no such comparison was located, but the binaries were not decompiled. The answers were tested instead: on 2026-11-25 the battery (99,985 vectors) and the targeted set (85,544) gave no mismatch on Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche and Celo, and the 200 large-offset vectors of offsets.py gave the specified word or failure on all four, on Celo pinned to the op-geth backend by batching each call between two web3_clientVersion requests. A wrong result in a mulmod, div, sdiv, smod or comparison would change FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48, 73), TickBitmap.compress (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26) or UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14), and none was seen.
findings.impact: None found. If some node code has the shape, nodes built from an affected toolchain would disagree with nodes built from a fixed one on that input; on BNB Chain and Polygon the validator set decides, and a disagreement would stall or fork followers rather than move PoolManager funds.
findings.preconditions: The operator builds with go1.26.6 to go1.26.10 or go1.27.3 (or a release in the variant range), and some function on the execution path contains the faulty comparison shape. Neither the shape in client code nor whether go1.26.11 fixed the issue was confirmed.
findings.mitigations: Node operators rebuild with a Go release whose notes name issue 82839 once one exists. The deployer reruns battery.py, targeted.py and offsets.py after each client rebuild. LPs need do nothing.

sources.supports: open prove miscompile, affected go1.26.6 to go1.26.10, go1.27.3 and master; variant from go1.24.13; caused to surface by the #80619 backport; fix CL 858581

sources.url: eth_call with state override on https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc and https://forno.celo.org, 2026-11-25 (results in research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/go/)

findings.title: Follower nodes on OP Mainnet, Base, Zora, World Chain, Celo, X Layer and reth-bsc validate blocks through an execution cache with the stale destroyed-account branch
findings.difference: celo-org/reth 74cc8bb, okx/reth 81573d2 and bnb-chain/reth 3b2bd02 keep the branch in insert_state that removes a destroyed account without original code and skips its storage (cached_state.rs lines 863-881, 904-922 and 863-881). The branch is harmful only if the cache already holds a storage word of that address.
findings.mechanism: Read for the three networks cycle 16 did not cover. celo-reth pins celo-org/revm bd28f94 (revm-database 13.0.1, revm-context 16.0.1, revm-context-interface 17.0.1, revm-handler 18.1.0), whose state, account status, journal and pre-execution files equal the crates.io releases byte for byte; reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix pins the same crates.io versions; xlayer-reth v0.0.7 pins revm-database 15.0.2, revm-context 18.0.3, revm-context-interface 19.0.3 and revm-handler 20.0.3. In all of them State::storage returns zero without a database read for LoadedNotExisting, InMemoryChange, Destroyed, DestroyedChanged and DestroyedAgain accounts (states/account_status.rs lines 58-67, states/state.rs lines 239-270 in 13.0.1 and 262-293 in 15.0.2), the journal returns zero without a read for an account created in the transaction (journaled_state/account.rs lines 172 and 205-209 in both), create_account_checkpoint marks the target created before init code runs (journal/inner.rs lines 511-540), and access lists only mark slots warm (pre_execution.rs lines 53-60). Since Cancun the destroyed codeless account was created in its block, so before creation it has no code and no frame can SLOAD it, and after creation the created flag answers zero. The only reth path that reads slots outside execution is the block access list prewarm (prewarm.rs lines 801-804 for Celo and BNB, the BAL pool at lines 405-420 for X Layer). It runs only when the payload carries a BAL, and none does: the OP execution data that Celo uses returns None from block_access_list (celo-org/optimism b08a8d0 rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/payload.rs lines 74-76; okx/optimism main, develop and dev return None at lines 69-71), and reth-bsc's BscExecutionData returns None (src/node/engine_api/validator.rs lines 325-327). No default path seeds the stale word, so followers cannot be stalled this way. The PoolManager is never on the branch (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364).
findings.impact: None today. The hazard returns if a block access list fork ships on a client that still has the old branch.
findings.preconditions: A block access list in the payload on a client with the old insert_state branch. No listed build has both.
findings.mitigations: Operators take a reth base with pull request 28148 before any block access list fork.

findings.title: Base and Celo block builders read through the reth execution cache that still has the stale branch for a destroyed account without code, when the operator enables cache sharing
findings.difference: Celo's endpoint still reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb. The builder reads through the execution cache only when share_execution_cache_with_payload_builder is set (default false, crates/engine/primitives/src/config.rs line 238).
findings.mechanism: With the flag on, the OP payload builder wraps the shared cache in CachedStateProvider and executes through revm State with bundle updates (celo-org/optimism b08a8d0 rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/builder.rs lines 355-368 and 565). It reads storage through the same State::storage and journal rules as block validation, adds no slot prefetch of its own, and does not write the cache; insert_state runs on the engine side after validation. The builder therefore takes no path the default does not, and the seeding read that F-133 lacks is missing here too. F-132 and F-133 rest on the same missing link and are both rated info.
findings.impact: None today. A block access list fork on the old branch would affect followers first (F-133).
findings.preconditions: Cache sharing on at the sequencer and a payload that carries a block access list. The second does not exist on Celo.
findings.mitigations: Operators take a reth base with pull request 28148 before any block access list fork.

sources.supports: builder reads through CachedStateProvider and State, lines 355-368 and 565

cleared.check: L-808, RUSTSEC-2025-0137: which functions of ruint 1.15.0 (hyper-evm-sync, revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0) and 1.16.0 (nanoreth f0cad31, hl-archive-node/revm fdf9b16, revm-interpreter 25.0.3) call reciprocal_mg10, and is the divisor normalised on the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD paths?
cleared.result: Yes on every path. reciprocal_mg10 is exported as reciprocal and called by reciprocal_2_mg10 (reciprocal.rs line 111), div_nx1_normalized and div_nx1 (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 39 and 75, 1.15.0 lines 27 and 62); reciprocal_2 is called by div_nx2_normalized, div_nx2, div_nxm_normalized and div_nxm (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 112 and 144, knuth.rs lines 35 and 120). The only non-test callers of those are algorithms::div (1.15.0 mod.rs lines 49-99) and div_inlined (1.16.0 mod.rs lines 56-107), which trim zero limbs, send one limb divisors with a one limb numerator to native division and route the rest to div_nx1, div_nx2 or div_nxm. Each of these shifts the divisor by its leading zeros before the reciprocal (small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144, knuth.rs lines 105-120) and calls the normalized variant only when the shift is zero. Uint::div_rem, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, reduce_mod, add_mod and mul_mod reach only those two entry points (div.rs and modular.rs of both tags). revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call wrapping_div and wrapping_rem after a zero check, add_mod and mul_mod directly, and / and % on absolute values in i256_div and i256_mod (arithmetic.rs lines 26-63 and 31-83, i256.rs lines 80-130 and 92-143); the hl-archive-node fork's arithmetic.rs, i256.rs and bitwise.rs equal the crates.io 25.0.3 files. The precondition d >= 2^63 therefore always holds, and FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 35, 48, 62-73, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 252), UnsafeMath (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14, 26) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26, 57-64) cannot hand it an unnormalised divisor.
cleared.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2025-0137.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.15.0.crate and ruint-1.16.0.crate (sha256 11256b5f and 9ecb38f8, the second equal to the checksum in nanoreth f0cad31 Cargo.lock); https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-25.0.3.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/revm/fdf9b16bdd4388a680c97440c6e7f085647ece01/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/arithmetic.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/Cargo.lock

cleared.check: Release-mode run of ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 on the division and modular vectors, called the way revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call them, against Python integers.
cleared.result: No wrong word. A Rust harness (research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/harness/src/main.rs) links each ruint version by path from the crates.io archives and runs DIV and MOD through wrapping_div and wrapping_rem with the handlers' zero check, SDIV and SMOD through a transcription of i256_div and i256_mod, ADDMOD and MULMOD through add_mod and mul_mod, and two sequences from the source: the 512 bit product and remainder of FullMath.mulDiv (two mul_mod calls, one by 2^256-1) and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp. 3,585,969 vectors: 106,769 from battery.py and targeted.py (every DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, MULDIV512 and DIVUP vector, including the 16,858 MULMOD and mulDiv vectors of the 1.21.0 equal-top-limb shape) and 3,479,200 new ones with divisors of every bit length 1 to 256 (every normalisation shift for one, two, three and four limb divisors), numerators of every limb count, 257 bit ADDMOD sums, 512 bit MULMOD products and FullMath shaped denominators. Both versions in release mode with debug assertions off, as the clients ship, gave 0 mismatches; the same builds with debug assertions on gave 0 mismatches and never tripped the d >= 2^63 assertion, which a direct call with d = 1 does trip (reciprocal.rs line 78 in 1.15.0, 79 in 1.16.0). A flipped output word is caught by the comparison.

cleared.check: L-806: in celo-reth (celo-org/revm bd28f94), X Layer reth v0.0.7 (revm-interpreter 37.0.3) and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix, does any default path put a storage word of an address without code into the reth execution cache before a block destroys and recreates it?
cleared.result: No. See the F-133 entry: State::storage and the journal answer created, not-existing and destroyed accounts without a read, access lists only warm, and the block access list prewarm, the only direct slot read, never runs because the OP and BSC payload types return no block access list. The X Layer reading uses okx/optimism main, develop and dev because the v0.0.7 submodule commit could not be read.

cleared.check: L-809: MegaETH blocks with PoolManager calls that leave no PoolManager log, blocks with PoolManager activity after 32,766,000, and at least 2,000 blocks with the pre-state anchored to the parent root, re-executed by the stateless validator e1618ed7 built in cycle 16.
cleared.result: All validated. Selection: Blockscout's txlistinternal for the PoolManager (34,355 value-carrying frames, 16,579 blocks) gave 402 blocks with a native settle and no PoolManager log in the cycle 16 set, 348 succeeded frames and 265 inside reverted parents; Blockscout's tokentx (76,414 ERC-20 transfers to or from the PoolManager in 43,663 blocks) gave 102 more, together 503; eth_getLogs from 32,766,001 to 32,805,930 gave 80 PoolManager logs in 71 blocks. Block-list mode on these 574 blocks: 574 validated. The Blockscout v2 internal transaction list, which also holds zero-value and failed frames, was paged from the head back to block 31,861,608 (67,000 frames): 662 further blocks held only failed PoolManager calls (7,059 failed calls and 192 static calls in 2,292 transactions, reverted unlocks), and all 662 validated. Anchored mode: three windows of 2,000 consecutive blocks in chain-following mode, each anchored at the hash of the block before it, so every witness pre-state is checked against the previous state root: 16,164,204 to 16,166,203 (215 PoolManager blocks), 27,428,471 to 27,430,470 (53) and 32,791,059 to 32,793,058 (13): 6,000 of 6,000 validated. 50 sampled no-log, failed-call and post-32,766,000 blocks were also run anchored one by one: 50 of 50. Not covered: zero-value failed PoolManager calls before block 31,861,608, which only the slow v2 list holds, and Blockscout reported that some internal transactions of the range were not yet indexed.

cleared.check: Task 4: do the Go releases that build bor v2.11.1, BNB Chain geth v1.8.2, avalanchego 1.15.3 and celo op-geth c7ed55b8 fall in the affected range of Go issues 79874 and 80517?
cleared.result: Not for the three go1.26.10 builds: the 1.26 backports #79876 (79874) and #80619 (80517) were closed on 2026-08-05 in the Go1.26.6 milestone, and go1.26.6 shipped on 2026-08-13, so go1.26.10 has both fixes. Celo's op-geth is built with go1.24.13, a branch that received neither backport; the 80517 root cause is older than the 1.25 branch, so it may be present. offsets.py was therefore run on all four: 200 vectors each, copy, load and hash offsets from 0 to 2^256-1, with 0 mismatches on Polygon, BNB Chain and Avalanche (five Polygon vectors first hit a rate limit and passed on retry) and 200 of 200 on Celo pinned to the op-geth backend. The battery and the targeted set also pass on the four endpoints (Celo's mixed endpoint, both backends). These builds instead fall in the range of the newer issue 82839, recorded as a finding.

leads.question: Does any function on the execution or state path of geth, bor, bsc, avalanchego, celo op-geth or Nitro compare a sign-extended 8, 16 or 32 bit value with a constant that does not fit that width (the shape of Go issue 82839), and which Go release first fixes 82839?
leads.why: Those binaries are built by toolchains in the stated range; the tests pass on the endpoints, but a disagreement between nodes built by different toolchains would show only on the input that hits the shape.

leads.question: Enumerate the zero-value failed PoolManager calls on MegaETH before block 31,861,608 (reverted unlocks, sync and clear without value) and re-execute their blocks with the stateless validator.
leads.why: This cycle found 662 such blocks in the last 944,000 blocks, none in the cycle 16 set; the older history is not covered.

leads.question: Which okx/optimism commit does xlayer-reth v0.0.7 pin as deps/optimism, and does its OpExecData return a block access list?
leads.why: The F-133 reading for X Layer used the okx/optimism branches, not the pinned submodule.

leadResults.answer: Every caller of reciprocal_mg10 and reciprocal_2_mg10 in ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 normalises the divisor first, the revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 handlers and the hl-archive-node fork reach only those callers, and 3,585,969 division and modular vectors give no wrong word in release builds of either version.

No default path on celo-reth, X Layer reth v0.0.7 or reth-bsc caches a storage word of a codeless address: revm answers created, not-existing and destroyed accounts without a read, and the block access list prewarm never runs because their payloads carry no block access list.

The builder with cache sharing on reads through the same revm State and journal rules and adds no slot prefetch, so it takes no path the default lacks. F-132 and F-133 rest on the same missing link and are both rated info.

574 blocks (503 with PoolManager calls or transfers but no PoolManager log, 71 after 32,766,000) and 662 blocks with only failed PoolManager calls validated in block-list mode, 6,000 consecutive blocks in three windows and 50 sampled blocks validated with the pre-state anchored to the parent root. Zero-value failed calls before 31,861,608 remain, carried as a new lead.
